name: Guardian cryptic crossword, Penguin book 7 No 55

book.title: The New Penguin Book of The Guardian Crosswords, volume 7

clue.text: Security before marriage is lighter with a black head

blocks.note: safety is freedom from danger, i.e. security
a match is a marriage, as in a good match

explanation.surface: A cautious suitor wants financial security before the wedding, and the clue then swerves to a striking device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply places the first word ahead of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the everyday kind of small wooden stick that strikes only on its box, used to light fires.

clue.text: One who tries embroidery?

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who samples or tastes things
second meaning: a piece of needlework showing off various stitches

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark suggests someone attempting needlework; in fact the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster samples food, and a traditional stitched panel displaying alphabet letters and patterns carries this name too.

clue.text: One who won't settle for a fishing boat

blocks.note: first meaning: a rootless person wandering from place to place
second meaning: a boat that fishes with drift nets

explanation.surface: A restless person refuses to accept a fishing boat as a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer without a fixed home shares its name with a vessel using nets that float with the tide.

clue.text: Sailors’ stew with highball from Liverpool

blocks.note: a lob is a ball hit high into the air
Scouse means from Liverpool, a city in northwest England

explanation.surface: A sailors' stew served alongside a whisky highball in a Liverpool pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'highball' looks like a drink but is read as a high ball in tennis; Liverpudlians are called Scousers, after this very stew.
explanation.definitionFit: This meat and vegetable hash was traditional ship's fare for seamen, and gave Liverpool people their nickname.

clue.text: Optimist’s view of fried egg coming up

blocks.note: first meaning: the bright aspect that a cheerful person looks on
second meaning: an egg fried with the yolk facing up is served this way up

explanation.surface: A cheerful person's outlook on the breakfast that is about to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: An egg 'sunny side up' is fried on one side only, yolk showing; 'coming up' supplies the up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopeful people look on the bright aspect of life, and the yolk face of an unturned fried egg has the same name.

clue.text: See 12
Trojan wife and mother in rendering of rock

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is enclosed by it, so the mother goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
roche is the French rendering, or translation, of rock
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A Trojan wife and mother appears in a performance of rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendering' looks like a performance but means a translation into French.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer she is Hector's devoted spouse in Troy and mother of Astyanax, the heroine of Euripides' tragedy.

clue.text: Area for playing tig before defilement?

blocks.note: first meaning: a playing field for touch, another name for the chasing game tig or tag
second meaning: the biblical saying that he who touches tar shall be defiled

explanation.surface: A children's playground game is followed by something sinister.
explanation.walkthrough: Ecclesiasticus says 'He that toucheth pitch shall be defiled', so touching the tar comes before the defilement. Tig is the British name for tag.
explanation.definitionFit: A field where tag is played can be called this, and handling tar is what proverbially comes ahead of being dirtied.

clue.text: Punish molester with short time? It takes money

indicators.note: to punish is to knock about, so these letters are beaten into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A call to sentence an offender to only a brief prison term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short time' looks like a lenient sentence but is just T.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin-operated meter accepts payment through a slit, for gas, electricity or parking.

clue.text: See 19
Policeman without pull in fortified dwelling

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so one word sits around the other

blocks.note: a peeler is an old name for a policeman, after Sir Robert Peel
to tow is to pull along

explanation.surface: A policeman lacking influence lives in a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' seems to mean lacking but means outside. Peel founded London's police, hence peelers and bobbies.
explanation.definitionFit: A small square fortified keep built on the Scottish and English borders to defend a family against raiders.

clue.text: Greek painter has copy to dispose of on return

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so this word is read from right to left

blocks.note: to ape is to copy
to sell something is to dispose of it

explanation.surface: A Greek painter must get rid of a forgery when it is sent back.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the most celebrated artist of ancient Greece, court portraitist to Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Indonesian painter follows complete with a model

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, an Indonesian island

blocks.note: a sum is a complete total
taken as written
the Model T was Ford's famous car
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: An Indonesian artist comes after a complete set with a model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'painter follows' puts RA after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the largest islands of the archipelago nation, it belongs to Indonesia.

clue.text: Artiste Tina Turner comes on stage in front of the Queen

indicators.note: the singer's surname is read as one who turns things about, so the name before it is rearranged

blocks.note: an actor coming on stage is said to enter
the name shuffled
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The singer Tina Turner walks out to perform before the Queen at a royal variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous singer's surname does the work: her first name gets turned.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional performer such as a singer or dancer, someone who amuses an audience.

clue.text: God jocularly supplies empty house or bed

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, bendily, so the following letters are flexed into a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written: all fifteen letters

explanation.surface: God, people joke, provides a vacant home or somewhere to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplies' looks like a verb meaning provides, but it is read as 'supply', the adverb from supple. The phrase echoes 'Somebody up there likes me'.
explanation.definitionFit: People speak humorously of a heavenly being watching over them with this phrase pointing skyward.

clue.text: Acid from leaves of caper? That’s not right

definitions.note: the answer is the adjective in folic acid

indicators.note: 'not right' asks for the letter standing for right to be taken away

blocks.note: a caper is a frolic, a playful escapade
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A sour substance squeezed from caper leaves turns out to be wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caper' looks like the pickled bud but means a romp.
explanation.definitionFit: This B vitamin was first isolated from spinach leaves, and its name comes from Latin folium, leaf.

clue.text: Sailor, one of five on Roman throne

definitions.note: the definition describes a person; the answer is a king

blocks.note: a tar is a sailor
a quin is one of quintuplets

explanation.surface: A sailor who is one of quintuplets ends up as Roman emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Two legendary kings of early Rome bore this name, the last being Tarquinius Superbus.

clue.text: Affectionate term used by Jason, say, on first of July?

indicators.note: say asks us to go by what is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: my dear is an affectionate term, and Jason's wife was Medea

explanation.surface: How Jason the Argonaut might address his beloved on the first day of July.
explanation.walkthrough: Jason calling his wife Medea sounds like him saying 'my dear'; both sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The start of July falls at roughly the halfway point of the calendar, half the twelve months gone.

clue.text: Book about paintings is hard going

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps around the second

blocks.note: a tome is a large book
oils are oil paintings

explanation.surface: An art book is heavy reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Work that is laborious and tiring calls for a great deal of strenuous effort.

clue.text: State of trouble and disappointment laid on?

blocks.note: the surface reading: being in trouble and having one's hopes dampened
the setter's reading: the plumbed supplies to taps in a house

explanation.walkthrough: To be in hot water is to be in trouble; to pour cold water on a plan is to disappoint it. Together they are what a modern house has laid on.
explanation.definitionFit: Houses advertise both heated and unheated supplies piped to the taps as standard amenities installed.

clue.text: Is charity an afterthought in the Bible?

definitions.note: describes the answer, a book of the Bible

blocks.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter
alms are charitable gifts

explanation.surface: A question asking whether scripture treats giving to the poor as an afterthought.
explanation.walkthrough: The afterthought comes first in the answer even though charity is named first.
explanation.definitionFit: This collection of 150 sacred songs forms one of the Old Testament books.

clue.text: Breakwater in body or vaulting, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase asks us to go by the pronunciation, not the spelling

blocks.note: a groin is part of the body and also the edge where two vaults meet

explanation.surface: A breakwater appears in a body of water or some arched structure.
explanation.walkthrough: The spoken word must fit both the anatomy and the architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: A low wall built out from a beach into the sea to check erosion and drifting sand.

clue.text: Wild throstle gets a few weeks’ residence

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters run riot into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wild song thrush takes up lodgings for a few weeks.
explanation.walkthrough: A throstle is an old word for the song thrush.
explanation.definitionFit: A rental arrangement lasting only briefly, such as a holiday apartment rented for a month.

clue.text: Boy takes punishment from male beast

blocks.note: Tom is a boy's name
the cat o' nine tails was a whip used as punishment

explanation.surface: A boy is punished by an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The term specifically names an uncastrated male feline, as opposed to a queen.

clue.text: Setter’s problem, one that constrains

blocks.note: the setter is 'I', so setter's is I'm, I am
a poser is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: A crossword setter confesses a difficulty with a restrictive person.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters refer to themselves as I or me; here the apostrophe-s is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who forces rules or burdens on others limits their freedom and compels them.

clue.text: Place for flowers in church, not so at first

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
else means otherwise, not so
the opening letter of at

explanation.surface: Flowers in a church, though not at the start of the service.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chelsea Flower Show is held every May in this London district.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Royal Horticultural Society show in southwest London makes the district synonymous with blooms.

clue.text: Put through hole in red hat?

indicators.note: a hat with a hole in it is damaged, so its letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cardinal's red hat has a hole that needs a needle and cotton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put through hole' looks like the definition, but the hole belongs to the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass a fine strand, cable or similar line along a narrow passage or eye.

clue.text: Some sanctimonious Athenian

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so just part of the next word is taken

blocks.note: found inside the word

explanation.surface: A self-righteous citizen of ancient Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Timon of Athens is the misanthrope who gives away his fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary misanthrope of classical Athens, hero of a Shakespeare play, came from that city.
